The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus (quaesumus Domine); 1962 sets Excita, quaesumus, Domine,; 1862 closes the petition with a full stop before Qui vivis; 1962 sets a colon (salvari:); 1862 sets 'in unitate Spiritus sancti Deus, per omnia'; 1962 sets 'in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus: per omnia' -- lower-case sancti, no comma before Deus, comma instead of colon after it; OCR noise in the 1862 layer, not textual: the ornamental E recognises as 'inXcita' / 'Pj' across 13231-13232, and 'liberante salvari' reads 'liberrinte salvdn'; OCR noise, not textual: the 1862 response sign at line 13240 recognises as 'JL Amen.' for R-with-bar Amen. Excita, quaesumus, Domine, potentiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminentibus
peccatorum nostrorum periculis, te mereamur protegente eripi, te liberante
salvari: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus:

propers.name: Epistle
propers.text:
Fratres: Scientes quia hora est jam nos de somno surgere. Nunc enim propior est
nostra salus, quam cum credidimus. Nox praecessit, dies autem appropinquavit.
Abjiciamus ergo opera tenebrarum, et induamur arma lucis. Sicut in die honeste
ambulemus: non in commessationibus et ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus et
impudicitiis, non in contentione et aemulatione: sed induimini Dominum Jesum
Christum.
